newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says rebel death toll in Iraq nears 1,000.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says rebel death toll in Iraq nears 1,000.

text.p: Turkey's armed forces have killed nearly 1,000 Kurdish separatists during a five-day-old incursion into northern Iraq, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported on Sunday.

Anatolian quoted sources at military headquarters as saying 998 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas had been killed and 141 captured. Clashes were intensifying in the regions of Sinaht and Zap, it said.
The military sources gave no details of troop casualties, but on Saturday they said 12 soldiers had been killed.

Journalists have been barred from the region by Turkish troops and their Iraqi Kurdish allies, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). Communications were blocked, making independent confirmation of the figures and other incidents impossible.

The pro-Kurdish MED-TV said more than 30 Turkish soldiers had been killed in fighting with the rebels. It made no mention of PKK casualties there, but said one guerrilla had been killed in clashes with soldiers in eastern Turkey, in which 15 troops died.

The channel said in a written statement the rebels had shot down two army helicopters on Sunday in the triangle of land between Zap, Avasin and Metin. A day earlier it said another helicopter had been downed in the region.
The Turkish operation against PKK guerrilla bases inside the Kurdish "safe haven" of northern Iraq has drawn criticism from Ankara's Western allies and the United Nations.
On Sunday, military headquarters said an army helicopter had crashed in northern Iraq after a "technical fault", killing two pilots.
"A helicopter belonging to the army crashed because of a technical fault on May 18 at 7:30 a.m. (0430 GMT) south of the Cukurca area of Hakkari province," the general staff said in a brief statement.
